title: The Montauk Oval
client: For Dana and Theo, a proposal at Ditch Plains
summary: A 2.1 carat oval on a knife-edge band with a hidden halo under the stone.
story: Theo came in with one photo and one rule: nothing that catches on a wetsuit. We kept the profile low, used four claw prongs, and tucked a hidden halo of twelve diamonds under the stone so it only shows from the side.
details: GIA report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: East River Emerald Cut
client: For Priyanka, who wanted it to read sideways
summary: A lab-grown emerald cut set east to west on a slim 18k yellow gold band.
story: Priyanka wanted something that looked like jewelry first and an engagement ring second. Setting the stone horizontally made it feel like an architectural bar. We chose a lab-grown stone so the budget could go into a heavier band.
details: IGI report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Fifth Avenue Cushion
client: For Rachel, after her grandmother's ring
summary: A cushion cut in a fine micro-pavé halo, sized to echo a 1950s family ring.
story: Rachel brought her grandmother's ring for reference. We measured its proportions, then rebuilt the idea in platinum with a halo that sits flush with the stone instead of standing proud of it.
details: GIA report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Bleecker Pear
summary: A 1.2 carat pear on a rose gold pavé band, pointed toward the fingertip.
story: Jordan asked for the point to face the fingertip, which lengthens the hand. A protective V prong guards the tip. The pavé runs halfway around the band so it stays comfortable for a climber.
details: IGI report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Tribeca Three Stone
summary: A 1.8 carat round between two tapered pears, one for each decade and the day itself.
story: Michael wanted a ring that told a story without a word on it. We matched two pear side stones for color and taper, then rotated them so their points lead the eye back to the center.
details: GIA report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Gramercy Marquise
client: For Elena, who loves old things
summary: A north-south marquise with milgrain edges and a hand-engraved gallery.
story: Elena collects Victorian lockets. We drew the gallery from one of them, then Elias hand-engraved the shoulders after casting. It took two extra weeks and was worth every day.
details: GIA report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Hudson Radiant
summary: A crisp 2.5 carat lab-grown radiant on a cathedral band in 18k white gold.
story: Marcus wanted size and sparkle without stretching his budget. A lab-grown radiant gave him both. Raised cathedral shoulders let a wedding band sit flush underneath.
details: IGI report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Chelsea Asscher
client: For a surgeon who wears gloves all day
summary: An Asscher cut in a full platinum bezel with nothing to snag.
story: Nadia needed a ring she could wear under gloves. A full bezel protects the corners of the Asscher. We softened the outer edge so it slides on and off cleanly.
details: GIA report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: SoHo Toi et Moi
client: For two people who could not pick one stone
summary: A pear and an oval side by side on a bypass band in 18k yellow gold.
story: Lea liked pears. Ana liked ovals. The toi et moi setting holds both, angled so they almost touch. We sourced the pair together so the color matches under any light.
details: GIA reports on file (numbers withheld in demo)

title: Kyoto Sapphire
summary: A cornflower oval sapphire in a diamond halo on a split shank.
story: Hana wanted color without it looking like costume jewelry. We showed her five sapphires side by side in daylight. She picked the softest blue, and the halo keeps it bright at night.
details: Lab report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Nolita Emerald
summary: A Colombian emerald reset between two diamond baguettes from her mother's ring.
story: Camila brought a ring with a cracked shank and a stone she loved. We removed the emerald, checked it under the scope, and rebuilt the setting around it with protective corners.

title: West Village Eternity
summary: A shared-prong eternity band of nineteen round diamonds, made to sit flush with her cushion halo.
story: We made this band the same week as her engagement ring so the two fit like one piece. Each stone is matched for color within one grade.

title: Brooklyn Bezel Pendant
summary: A 0.8 carat bezel-set round on a fine cable chain in 18k yellow gold.
story: Something to wear every day, including in the shower. The bezel is closed at the back to keep it clean and the chain is adjustable at 16 and 18 inches.
details: IGI report on file (number withheld in demo)

title: Upper East Studs
summary: A matched pair of one carat rounds in four-prong martini settings.
story: Matching studs is harder than it looks. Priya sourced six candidate pairs and we compared them under the same lamp until two stones looked like twins.
details: GIA reports on file (numbers withheld in demo)

title: Harlem Pear Drops
summary: Lab-grown pear drops in halos, hung from small round studs in rose gold.
story: Worn once on the day and then every Friday night after. We kept them light so they move when she does.
details: IGI reports on file (numbers withheld in demo)

title: Park Slope Princess
summary: A one carat princess cut held by V prongs on a squared band.
story: Ben wanted something modern and a little geometric. A princess cut, square shoulders and V prongs at each corner keep the whole ring in one clean language.
